items.followUp: Write the chemical formulae of carbon dioxide and common salt.

rubric.why: Identifies the chemical formula of water.
rubric.description: Water has the chemical formula H₂O.

rubric.why: Identifies the formula of sucrose, the common table sugar.
rubric.description: Sugar (sucrose) has the chemical formula C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ or identifying sugar as sucrose.

modelAnswer: The chemical formula of water is H₂O.
The chemical formula of sugar (sucrose) is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.

items.followUp: What is the nature of charge on protons?

rubric.why: Identifies cathode rays as a stream of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cathode rays consist of electrons.

rubric.why: States the charge carried by cathode rays.
rubric.description: Electrons carry a negative charge, so cathode rays are negatively charged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cathode rays carry a negative charge.

modelAnswer: Since electrons are negatively charged, cathode rays carry a negative charge.

items.followUp: How is nuclear fission used to generate electricity in a nuclear power plant?

rubric.why: Identifies U-235 as the nuclear fuel.
rubric.description: Uranium-235 is used as fuel in a nuclear reactor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying uranium-235 (U-235) as the fuel.

rubric.why: Explains how fission energy is converted into electrical energy.
rubric.description: Fission releases heat that produces steam; the steam drives a turbine connected to an electricity generator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that fission releases heat, or for describing steam driving a turbine to generate electricity.

modelAnswer: Uranium-235 is used as fuel in a nuclear reactor.
Its nuclei undergo fission, releasing heat that produces steam; the steam drives a turbine connected to an electricity generator.

items.followUp: What is meant by effective nuclear charge?

rubric.why: Identifies the electrons responsible for shielding.
rubric.description: Inner-shell (core) electrons cause the shielding effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inner-shell electrons as the cause of shielding.

rubric.why: Defines shielding in terms of reduced nuclear attraction on outer electrons.
rubric.description: Shielding effect is the reduction in the attractive force of the nucleus on outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding reduces the nuclear attraction experienced by outer electrons.

modelAnswer: The shielding effect is the reduction in the attractive force of the nucleus on the outer-shell electrons.
It is caused by the inner-shell electrons lying between the nucleus and the outer electrons.
